events.summary: H1 stands as the best-supported origin, and the residual uncertainties are now lower-confidence caveats rather than an unresolved competing origin. Grounding: every hop rests on verified findings — the only change adjacent to onset is dep-5905 (F3/F13/F36/F38, code-only, no config/flag), the new account_id+executed_at trades query executes as a Seq Scan over ~48.2M rows attributed to application_name=portfolio-service (F11, F27), and that fingerprint is verified absent for the entire preceding 30+h (F25, F26). Temporal order is tight and per-minute: deploy 08:56:00Z -> single-minute ledger-db transition at 08:58 across CPU 32->96%, slow_queries 1.3->139/min, connections 60->185 (F28), first Seq Scan log 08:58:38 (F11) -> order-service pool step and p99 step simultaneously at 08:59 (F42, F43) -> first INSERT statement-timeout ERROR 09:00:42 (F12). The 08:45 bucket's apparent early onset was an averaging artifact (F29). Alternatives were tested, not dismissed: H2 is positively weakened on five independent signals (unchanged autovacuum cadence, audit_log target not trades, no analyze change, flat CPU/disk across 08:00-08:54, discontinuity at 08:58), and its decisive vacuum/bloat/IOPS series are a permanent data-source limitation (F19) — not something this round could have closed; H3/H4 are contradicted on simultaneity and ordering; the coincident flag-flip path was closed by direct query (F35-F39). Scope: the asymmetry at co-tenants is explained by workload class — only order-service's INSERT INTO orders write class is cancelled (F12), co-tenants show zero ERROR/WARN-timeout signatures and flat error_rate (F31-F33) — and needs_evidence cannot fix this, since the co-tenant pool/wait and WARN series are permanently unavailable or budget-exhausted. I accept, with confidence capped at 0.72 rather than H1's 0.68-0.80+ because three stated items remain unverified and are carried as assumptions rather than evidence: (a) the 08:58 saturation's sole load contributor is inferred from a 100% single-fingerprint log census with truncated=true (F27) rather than a grouped per-application slow-query count, which is not obtainable (no dimensioned metric); (b) whether 45-52 db_pool_in_use was true pool exhaustion or elevated-but-healthy occupancy is undetermined because order-service exposes no pool_size/queue-depth series (F40, permanent limitation); (c) the co-tenants' non-degradation is attributed to workload class without their pool/wait metrics. None of these would change the fix (index the new trades query / revert dep-5905, per HIST-111 precedent F6/F17), which is why I accept rather than call it inconclusive.

critiques.summary: H1 stands as the best-supported origin, and the residual uncertainties are now lower-confidence caveats rather than an unresolved competing origin. Grounding: every hop rests on verified findings — the only change adjacent to onset is dep-5905 (F3/F13/F36/F38, code-only, no config/flag), the new account_id+executed_at trades query executes as a Seq Scan over ~48.2M rows attributed to application_name=portfolio-service (F11, F27), and that fingerprint is verified absent for the entire preceding 30+h (F25, F26). Temporal order is tight and per-minute: deploy 08:56:00Z -> single-minute ledger-db transition at 08:58 across CPU 32->96%, slow_queries 1.3->139/min, connections 60->185 (F28), first Seq Scan log 08:58:38 (F11) -> order-service pool step and p99 step simultaneously at 08:59 (F42, F43) -> first INSERT statement-timeout ERROR 09:00:42 (F12). The 08:45 bucket's apparent early onset was an averaging artifact (F29). Alternatives were tested, not dismissed: H2 is positively weakened on five independent signals (unchanged autovacuum cadence, audit_log target not trades, no analyze change, flat CPU/disk across 08:00-08:54, discontinuity at 08:58), and its decisive vacuum/bloat/IOPS series are a permanent data-source limitation (F19) — not something this round could have closed; H3/H4 are contradicted on simultaneity and ordering; the coincident flag-flip path was closed by direct query (F35-F39). Scope: the asymmetry at co-tenants is explained by workload class — only order-service's INSERT INTO orders write class is cancelled (F12), co-tenants show zero ERROR/WARN-timeout signatures and flat error_rate (F31-F33) — and needs_evidence cannot fix this, since the co-tenant pool/wait and WARN series are permanently unavailable or budget-exhausted. I accept, with confidence capped at 0.72 rather than H1's 0.68-0.80+ because three stated items remain unverified and are carried as assumptions rather than evidence: (a) the 08:58 saturation's sole load contributor is inferred from a 100% single-fingerprint log census with truncated=true (F27) rather than a grouped per-application slow-query count, which is not obtainable (no dimensioned metric); (b) whether 45-52 db_pool_in_use was true pool exhaustion or elevated-but-healthy occupancy is undetermined because order-service exposes no pool_size/queue-depth series (F40, permanent limitation); (c) the co-tenants' non-degradation is attributed to workload class without their pool/wait metrics. None of these would change the fix (index the new trades query / revert dep-5905, per HIST-111 precedent F6/F17), which is why I accept rather than call it inconclusive.

challenges.issue: Mechanism of scope rests on an unmeasured inference: the claim that co-tenants were spared because only order-service issues the cancelled INSERT write class is not backed by any measurement of payment-/settlement-service DB traffic, statement_timeout config, or their pool wait metrics (F40 permanent limitation; their pool/WARN series budget-exhausted). Severity: minor-to-major, because it does not affect the identified origin or fix (the offending workload is undeniably the portfolio-service trades Seq Scan), but it means the 'asymmetric blast radius' explanation remains an assumption.

Load attribution to the Seq Scan alone rests on a log census that is truncated=true (F27); the pre-window ~1/min slow queries were never logged or dimensioned, so 'single-fingerprint, 100% contribution' is approximated rather than counted. No dimensioned slow-query metric exists (permanent). Severity: minor — the fingerprint's novelty is independently verified (F25/F26), and no other new workload or change exists in the window (F3/F13/F36).

Retained at 0.15 with its causal direction already self-contradicted by the ordering (DB-side saturation 08:58 precedes the pool step 08:59, F28/F42; and it must explain the new Seq Scan fingerprint it cannot account for). Not blocking: H5 is properly ranked second and its own assumptions concede the ordering objection.

Dismissal of cfg-2903 rests partly on absent dedicated vacuum/IOPS series (F19) rather than direct refutation; however the four available signals (cadence F20, target F21, no-analyze F22, flat CPU/disk to 08:54 F23/F24) plus the 08:58 discontinuity are sufficient to rank it below H1, and the missing series are permanently unavailable. Severity: minor.
